newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka may soon move to 0.5 pct gasoil - CPC.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka may soon move to 0.5 pct gasoil - CPC.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) said on Wednesday it may soon bow to pressure from environmentalists to reduce the maximum sulphur content in its gas oil (diesel) to 0.5 percent from the current 1.0 percent.
The chairman of the state oil company, Anil Obeyesekere, said price considerations had been an obstacle to the change in the past because lower sulphur gas oil was more expensive.
Sri Lanka imported just under 600,000 tonnes of gas oil in 1996 in a series of tenders and is expected to buy some 690,000 tonnes this year, he said.

"There is an environmental lobby here to get low sulphur content diesel into our country but price is a factor which is inhibiting us. But certainly as time goes on we will have to give way to the environmentalists," he told Reuters in an interview.
"In the years to come we will have to comply with this requirement...maybe in about a year or so. I can't give a definite time frame."

Obeyesekere said Sri Lanka could reduce the content of its gas oil by changing its import requirements or by removing sulphur from gas oil at its own 50,000-60,000 barrels per day refinery at Sapugaskanda, north of the capital Colombo.
"We have a project for desulphurisation of diesel of 300 million rupees," but added, "It is at the stage of discussion."
He said importing low sulphur crudes was not a likely option, partly because it would require a reconfiguration of CPC's refinery. He gave no further details.
"I think we wouldn't move in that direction," he said.
